result.abstractText: The application of mRNA therapy is constrained by the current lipid nanoparticles' (LNPs) inability to target non-liver tissues. In this study, we demonstrate that ionizable lipids equipped with branched and biodegradable tails enhance the selective delivery of mRNA to the spleen, particularly to antigen-presenting cells. This approach offers novel insights into how the chemical structure of LNPs influences their organ-specific targeting capabilities.
